Enter the server address first, e.g. https://…/v1.
The %1$s API key is removed. The AI is off.
The address must start with https:// (or http://), e.g. https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1.
A model name may only hold lower-case letters, digits, dots and hyphens.
A model name may not hold spaces.

The scan isn\'t on yet. Add an API key for one of the AIs first (Gemini is the easiest). Then Scan with AI (the + button at the bottom centre) opens the camera: shoot every side, then tap Scan with AI.

The AI reads a photo of the card or the car and fills in the form. Photos are only sent when you ask the AI to read them. The AIs are tried from top to bottom: when one runs out of quota, is busy or takes too long, the same photos go straight to the next.

resources.string: A free daily quota from Google. When one model is busy or out of quota, other Gemini models are tried before moving to the next AI.
Free and very fast (about 1,000 requests a day). Each request takes 3 photos at most; the others are left out.
Free on the Experiment plan (needs a phone number check). On the free plan, Mistral may use the photos you send to train its models.
Free models: 50 requests a day (1,000 a day after a one-time $10 top-up). The openrouter/free model picks a free model that can read photos by itself.
Leave empty if the server needs no key
Free: 10,000 neurons a day on your own Cloudflare account, reset at midnight UTC. Needs your account ID (on the Workers AI page of the dashboard) and an API token with the Workers AI permission.
Free for trying things out with an NVIDIA Developer account (about 40 requests a minute). NVIDIA logs what is sent and may use it to improve its products. Pick a model that can read photos (vision).
GLM-4.6V-Flash from Z.ai (Zhipu AI) is free, one request at a time. Sign up with an email, no credit card.
No account and no key: about 2 requests a minute per model from each phone, anonymously. Good as the last one to try. Off until you switch it on.
Another service that speaks the OpenAI API format, such as a server on your own network. Pick a model that can read photos.
An account ID is 32 letters and digits (0–9, a–f).
